lines: If you get trapped in a blizzard on the highway, do not try to walk away.
Cole sits stranded in his car as a massive wall of white snow swallows the road.
Heavy snow piles against the doors while the freezing night temperature drops rapidly below zero.
Rescuers will search the highway, but Cole must survive the next 12 freezing dark hours.
One. Stay with the car because it provides shelter and makes you easier to find.
Walking out into blinding whiteout conditions guarantees you will become lost and freeze to death.
Two. Clear snow from your exhaust pipe before you ever turn on the vehicle engine.
A blocked exhaust pipe fills your closed cabin with lethal, odorless carbon monoxide gas quickly.
Run the engine about 10 minutes each hour for heat while cracking a window slightly.
Three. Tie a bright cloth to your antenna or car door to signal passing crews.
Turn on your inside dome light at night so emergency rescue teams can spot you.
Cole secures his bright cloth, clears the pipe, and settles in under his warm jacket.
He runs the engine for 10 minutes, cracks the window, and checks his dashboard clock.
It was the perfect survival plan, and rescue crews were finally approaching down the highway.
There was just one massive problem that Cole did not notice until this very second.
A heavy snowplow is barreling down his exact lane, blind to his buried, silent car.
part1.cliffhanger: A massive snowplow is speeding directly toward Cole's buried car without seeing it.
